items.label: Support External API
items.purpose: Let one VexLife Home intentionally select local or external Partner model realization while VexLife remains the owner of Conversation, Memory, contextual ground, capability admission and durable turn truth; add truthful provider connection, credential, availability, failure, privacy and qualification semantics; prove the body deterministically without paid API access; and keep real provider qualification as an explicit later gate.

items.label: A0 — Provider-neutral Companion inference seam
items.purpose: Re-ground the current Direct Companion circuit and form the smallest provider-neutral inference boundary that preserves current local mlx-lm behavior exactly while separating Vex-facing prepared messages, capability offer, generation intent, progress/cancellation and normalized result/evidence from the current numeric-loopback-only provider realization. At the 2026-11-23 checkpoint, current-main Warm Boot PR #518 owns overlapping DirectCompanionConnection/test paths, so overlapping mutation is held while provider-neutral contract analysis and disjoint proof planning continue; older #442/#383 remain provenance, not current mutation ownership.

items.label: A1 — Settings Local / Partner model-source topology
items.purpose: Evolve the existing Models human relationship so Local / Partner is first a presentation filter over canonical model offerings rather than a second durable model-choice truth. Each model row carries its source relationship (LOCAL or PARTNER(providerRef)); exact model Select/Use remains the semantic choice. Local rows keep artifact/runtime controls, Partner rows consume A2 Provider Connection/model-access truth and expose only lawful remote controls. Persist a separate source preference only if later Product pressure proves independent meaning.

items.label: A2 — Partner Provider Connection + credential/account/model contract
items.purpose: Form one truthful Partner connection relationship covering provider identity, source-owned built-in endpoint/dialect, protected host credential custody by opaque credentialRef, optional provider-specific non-secret account scope, account/service state, provider-visible model offerings and exact invocation qualification without placing secret values in Conversation, Memory, Context, logs, Git or Workgraph. Product #558 source-forms connection standing, provider catalog, no-JVM-secret credential custody, and VexLifePartnerAccountScope; Anthropic may carry an explicit wrkspc_ workspace coordinate only when the credential is not already scoped, while OpenAI/Kimi reject that coordinate. Platform host execution remains separately unproved.

items.label: A3 — OpenAI / Anthropic / Kimi provider adapters
items.purpose: Implement bounded provider realizations that translate the provider-neutral Companion contract into each provider's current request, authentication, streaming, reasoning/content and tool-call/result grammar, then normalize the result back into Vex-owned meaning without spreading vendor wire semantics through Conversation, Memory or capability owners. Product PR #554 now source-forms a provisional pure wire-codec body for OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages and Kimi Chat Completions on disjoint paths, including exact provider-call identity preservation/result carriage; A3 remains dependency-held because network/credential/provider-session integration still requires A0/A2 and exact JVM execution is owed.

items.label: A4 — Preserve Vex context, Capability Bridge and effective capabilities across providers
items.purpose: Prove that provider switching changes only the model/provider realization: canonical Conversation, Memory, Foundation, bounded prompt context and Capability Atlas/Bridge remain Vex-owned; provider-native tool requests converge into the same canonical Vex capability meaning; and effective capability availability is joined from exact connection/model/adapter/Product qualification rather than model names or marketing claims. Preserve the exact provider-native call identity (OpenAI call_id, Anthropic tool_use.id, Kimi tool_call.id) across the Bridge result continuation as bounded carriage evidence without making that provider ID capability/effect/Conversation authority.

items.label: A5 — Provider failure, availability and retry semantics
items.purpose: Normalize provider-specific status plus machine error type/code/body and stream-terminal evidence into truthful Vex meanings for invalid credentials, billing/quota holds, permission/model access, rate limits, overload, provider unavailability, invalid requests, context limits, malformed responses and interrupted streams; expose human controls without automatic cross-provider fallback or unsafe replay. Product #560 now source-forms a provisional no-effect mapping from P1 failure meaning into A2 connection currentness, including conservative UNKNOWN service standing for ambiguous stream/response failures and exact provider-identity binding. Acceptance remains dependency-held on current P1/A2 source and exact JVM proof.

items.label: A6 — Credential, context-egress, tool-admission and replay security boundary
items.purpose: Use the existing Vex Security Assurance question owner to source-place minimum invariants for provider/credential identity, secret custody, bounded remote context egress, tool admission, replay/fallback and evidence. Platform-neutral #561 keeps secrets out of JVM read paths and defines the native host protocol/client. Windows #562 now source-forms Credential Manager + redirect-denying HTTPS and a no-API synthetic host proof runner; macOS #563 source-forms Security.framework Keychain + redirect-refusing URLSession and a no-API proof runner that compiles the exact Swift helper first. Native OS execution, packaging identity and lived helper protocol proof remain owed; provider-hosted/mutating tools and automatic fallback stay held.

items.label: A7 — Zero-cost deterministic provider conformance
items.purpose: Exercise exact provider request/stream/tool/failure fixtures through injected transports and local harnesses so the external-provider consumer body, Settings state, effective capabilities, secret redaction, turn failure semantics and no-fallback laws can be proven without paid API calls; keep all real-provider availability and billing claims explicitly unestablished. Product PR #553 now forms the P0 official-doc-conformant request/response/stream/tool/error fixture corpus and JVM fixture-integrity source on disjoint paths; connected readback proves fixture structure while JVM execution remains owed. A7 itself stays dependency-held until the A0/A1/A2/A3/A4/A5/A6 implementation relationships exist.

items.label: A8 — Real external provider qualification
items.purpose: After deterministic conformance is accepted, run the smallest bounded real provider/model round trip needed to prove the exact credential/account/model/stream/tool relationship claimed live-qualified. This work remains held until a legitimate usable provider credential/account/credit or an explicitly accepted equivalent is available. The Product may still reach an accepted CONTRACT_PROVEN/LIVE_UNQUALIFIED production posture before this gate when release authority accepts it, provided the UI exposes a small accessible information affordance that says live provider validation is pending and does not claim live qualification.

items.label: A9 — Lived local ↔ Partner model switching with one Vex continuity
items.purpose: Prove the human can switch among qualified local and Partner models while one canonical Vex Home, Conversation, Memory and capability relationship persists; each turn reconstructs bounded provider-ready ground through the selected adapter; provider-side history/cache remains execution detail; and failures never cause silent provider fallback or duplicate turn effects.
